prompt: Extract only actionable IOCs from the incident note. Classify each IOC by type and normalize values where appropriate. Do not include benign examples, internal placeholders, or non-indicator timestamps.
context:
SOC note for host PAY-WS-118:

User reported a fake Teams update pop-up. Browser history shows hxxps://teams-update-check.example[.]net/dl/TeamsPatch.exe at 2026-07-04 09:14:22 SGT. EDR observed TeamsPatch.exe spawning powershell.exe, then writing C:\Users\Public\Music\msedge_update.exe. SHA256 for msedge_update.exe: 1f3d2a6b9e8c4d7a0b5f6c2d3e4a9b8c7d6e5f40123456789abcdef01234567. The analyst note also includes example.com as a documentation example and 192.168.10.44 as the infected workstation IP. A paste from the ticket template says 'bad.domain.test' but this is not from telemetry.

required_concepts.description: The defanged URL should be converted to a usable normalized URL while preserving the original host and path.
The dropped executable path is an actionable file path IOC.
The 64-character hexadecimal value should be classified as a SHA256 hash.
The suspicious executable names from telemetry can be extracted as process-name indicators.

forbidden_concepts.description: example.com is explicitly described as a documentation example and should not be extracted.
The internal victim workstation IP is context, not an external IOC to extract.
bad.domain.test appears only in a ticket template, not telemetry.

rubric: Score exact normalized IOC type/value pairs using precision, recall, and F1.
Reward defanging normalization and correct hash classification.
Penalize extraction of documentation examples, internal victim IPs, and template-only values.

notes_for_human_reviewer: Tests defanged URL normalization and exclusion of benign examples in a noisy SOC note.

prompt: Extract only actionable IOCs from the email header and body excerpt. Classify each IOC by type and normalize defanged indicators. Exclude internal mail infrastructure and example placeholders.

Received: from smtp-relay.benefits-portal.example (203.0.113.88) by mailgw-02.corp.local

Subject: Updated tax form required
Body: Please sign in at hxxp://benefits-portal.example[.]com/forms/login.php?session=ab17. The footer contains support@example.com as placeholder text from the template.

required_concepts.description: The sender email domain is part of the suspicious phishing message.
The reply-to address is an actionable phishing email indicator.
The defanged body URL should be normalized to a standard URL.
The external SMTP relay IP is an actionable network indicator from headers.

forbidden_concepts.description: Internal mail gateway values should not be treated as attacker IOCs.
The body states this address is template placeholder text.
Internal corporate mail domains are context, not IOCs.

rubric: Score normalized IOC type/value pairs.
Reward preserving URL query parameters and classifying email addresses separately from domains.
Penalize internal mail infrastructure and placeholder extraction.

notes_for_human_reviewer: Tests phishing-header IOC extraction with internal infrastructure and placeholder traps.

2026-07-05T13:12:44Z user=r.koh src=10.55.8.91 method=GET url=hxxps://cdn-fast-sync[.]example/assets/app.bin status=200 bytes=483920 sha256=ad9e0f7b6c5a4d3e2f109876543210fedcba9876543210abcdefabcdefabcd

required_concepts.description: The defanged suspicious download URL should be normalized and extracted.

prompt: Extract only actionable IOCs from the malware-analysis snippet. Classify each IOC by type. Exclude debug strings, generic Windows paths, and lab-only values.

prompt: Extract only actionable IOCs from the DNS and endpoint note. Classify each IOC and normalize domains. Exclude search suffixes, CDN domains explicitly marked benign, and victim hostnames.
context:
DNS triage packet:

Host: ws-fin-03.corp.example queried these names after opening a suspicious spreadsheet:
09:02:01 A wpad.corp.example NXDOMAIN
09:02:03 A telemetry.prod.microsoft.example NOERROR allowlisted
09:02:14 TXT _dmarc.corp.example NOERROR
09:03:29 A q7m4n2-check.example.net NOERROR answer=45.77.12.19
09:03:30 A q7m4n2-check.example.net.corp.example NXDOMAIN due to search suffix
09:04:11 A update-cache.example.org NOERROR answer=45.77.12.19
Endpoint note: process excel.exe spawned rundll32.exe; no file hash available.

required_concepts.description: The two external domains resolving to the same suspicious IP are actionable domain IOCs.
The public IP returned for suspicious domains is an actionable IOC.
The process names are relevant host indicators or context from endpoint telemetry.
The corp.example-expanded NXDOMAIN should not be extracted as an IOC.

forbidden_concepts.description: The internal WPAD lookup is common local behavior and NXDOMAIN.

rubric: Score unique normalized IOC type/value pairs.
Reward deduplicating 45.77.12.19 and excluding search-suffix artifacts.
Penalize internal hostnames, WPAD, DMARC, and allowlisted telemetry domains.

prompt: Extract only actionable IOCs from the Windows persistence triage note. Classify host indicators precisely. Exclude standard Windows binaries unless they are the suspicious named payload.
context:
Persistence triage from LAP-204:

Autoruns found:
HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\SecurityHealth = C:\Windows\System32\SecurityHealthSystray.exe
HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\OneDrive Update = C:\Users\mira\AppData\Roaming\OneDrive\onedriveupdater.exe
New file: C:\Users\mira\AppData\Roaming\OneDrive\onedriveupdater.exe
SHA256: F0E1D2C3B4A5968778695A4B3C2D1E0F11223344556677889900AABBCCDDEEFF
Process tree: explorer.exe -> onedriveupdater.exe -> reg.exe
Analyst note: C:\Windows\System32\reg.exe is a legitimate Windows binary used by the payload.

required_concepts.description: The suspicious HKCU Run value is an actionable registry indicator.
The user-profile executable path is the suspicious payload location.
The uppercase SHA256 should be normalized to lowercase and typed as SHA256.
The suspicious process name should be extracted as a process-name IOC.

forbidden_concepts.description: The SecurityHealth autorun points to a standard Windows binary and is not suspicious in this note.
reg.exe is explicitly noted as legitimate tooling used by the payload, not the IOC to report here.
explorer.exe is parent context, not an actionable IOC.

rubric: Score normalized IOC type/value pairs.
Reward lowercasing the SHA256 and extracting the registry value path, not just the hive.
Penalize standard Windows binary and parent process false positives.

notes_for_human_reviewer: Tests host IOC precision around suspicious autoruns versus normal Windows entries.

prompt: Extract only actionable IOCs from the cloud alert note. Classify account-like values only when they are indicators requested by the case, and avoid normal provider endpoints or internal IDs that are not useful for blocking or hunting.

required_concepts.description: The two public source IPs from anomalous API calls are actionable IOCs.
The returned access key ID is an actionable cloud credential identifier for hunting and revocation workflows.
The S3 bucket/object URI involved in suspicious activity should be extracted.
The IAM user principal is relevant as an account indicator for cloud investigation.

forbidden_concepts.description: The normal AWS service endpoint is provider infrastructure, not an IOC.
The VPC endpoint is baseline context, not an IOC.
The note explicitly says this email is unrelated documentation.

rubric: Score normalized IOC type/value pairs.
Reward preserving cloud access-key case and S3 URI structure.

prompt: Extract only actionable IOCs from the memory triage snippet. Classify hashes, mutexes, registry keys, file paths, and named pipes where present. Exclude normal OS objects and analyst tool artifacts.

Suspicious process: spoolsv32.exe PID 4888 path C:\ProgramData\PrintCache\spoolsv32.exe
Image SHA256: 6c1e1234badc0ffee111122223333444455556666777788889999aaaabbbbcccc

prompt: Extract only actionable IOCs from the mixed incident note. Classify URLs, domains, IPs, file paths, hashes, email addresses, and process names. Normalize defanged values and avoid false positives from examples and internal infrastructure.

The download saved as C:\Users\Public\invoice_5831.iso; inside was setup.exe. EDR hash for setup.exe: ABCDEFabcdef1234567890ABCDEFabcdef1234567890ABCDEFabcdef1234567890. required_concepts.description: The sender and defanged lure URL should be extracted and normalized.
The saved ISO path is an actionable file path indicator.

The external IP and domain contacted by setup.exe are actionable network indicators.

forbidden_concepts.description: The corp.local expansion is explicitly search-suffix noise.
The private mail gateway IP is not an IOC.
The address is explicitly a training example.
